newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends volatile session firmer.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends volatile session firmer.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures finished higher in choppy dealings on Thursday, boosted by commission house shortcovering, dealers said.

May rose 1.35 cents per lb on the day, to end at 191.05 cents, after trading from 192.25 to 185.00. Second-month July settled 0.65 cents firmer, at 173.80 cents, while the back months closed up 0.85 to 2.10.
Traders said much of the day's focus was on the nearby May/July switch, which widened to 17.25 cents today from 16.55 cents at the close on Wednesday.
Operators were beginning to get out of their May positions ahead of first notice day on April 22, they said. Open interest in May was down 323 lots Wednesday, to 10,878 lots.
Total open interest, however, rose 1,183 lots to 34,221 lots as of Wednesday.

Technically, after filling a chart gap from 190.50 to 192.00 today in the May contract, traders said the next upside objective would be the 195.00 level, followed by 200.00. On the downside, support was seen near 187.00.
On the fundamental side, traders said a strike by Colombian truckers set for April 20 would probably provide underlying support.

Industry sources in Colombia said on Thursday coffee exporters have begun rushing to get shipments to port ahead of the strike. They said about 420,000 70-kilo bags were being shipped out ahead of schedule in a bid to ensure that April export deadlines would not be missed.

Elsewhere, coffee stocks held by Brazilian cooperatives totaled 1.49 million 60.5-kg bags on March 31, National Coffee Council said in a statement. That was down from than the 2.07 million bags held by cooperatives as of Feb 28 and also below the 1.75 million bags held at the same stage in 1996.
After Thursday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks were off 250 60-kg bags, to 81,328 bags as of April 8. There were no bags pending grading, the exchange said.
Volume reached an estimated 10,295 lots, down slightly from Wednesday's official tally of 11,288 lots.
